edges.mechanism: Metformin reduces ileal calcium-dependent IF-B12 uptake; serum B12 falls ~19% vs placebo with dose- and duration-dependent deficiency risk.
edges.evidence: RCT (4.3 y, NNH 13.8), DPPOS (OR 1.13/yr), 3 MAs (OR 2.45-2.95); ADA and MHRA recommend periodic B12 monitoring; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Gastric acid suppression impairs release of protein-bound food B12; supplemental crystalline B12 is unaffected.
edges.evidence: Large case-control (>=2 y use OR 1.65); MA OR 1.42 with heterogeneity; 2025 MA null; NICE lists as risk factor; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Acid suppression reduces food-B12 release.
edges.evidence: Case-control OR 1.25 for >=2 y supply; NICE risk-factor list; low certainty

edges.mechanism: N2O oxidizes cob(I)alamin and inactivates methionine synthase, producing functional deficiency (raised tHcy/MMA) with often-normal serum B12; myeloneuropathy.
edges.evidence: Systematic review of 574 recreational users, adolescent case series/SR, poison-centre trends; NICE: test tHcy/MMA first

edges.mechanism: Colchicine causes reversible B12 malabsorption (reduced ileal IF-B12 receptor in animal model).
edges.evidence: Clinical mechanistic study, animal data, label and NICE risk-factor list; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Methylcobalamin reduced capecitabine-induced hand-foot syndrome without significant change in capecitabine dose reductions.
edges.evidence: Phase 3 RCT (n=234): grade>=2 HFS 14.5% vs 29.1%

edges.mechanism: Duplicate cobalamin dosing; no benefit of excess B12 without deficiency and observational signals with very high intakes (hip fracture with B6, acneiform eruptions).
edges.evidence: Review and observational/case data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Duplicate B12 (and B6/folate) dosing; combined high B6+B12 intake associated with hip fracture and rosacea/acneiform eruptions.
edges.evidence: Nurses' Health Study cohort (RR 1.47) and case reports

edges.mechanism: High combined B6 (>=35 mg/d) + B12 (>=20 ug/d) intake associated with hip fracture; high-dose B6+B12 linked to rosacea fulminans/acneiform eruptions.
edges.evidence: Prospective cohort (n=75,864) and case reports; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Folate and B12 jointly lower homocysteine, but high folate can correct anemia while B12 neuropathy progresses; high folate with low B12 linked to worse anemia/cognition and higher MMA/tHcy.
edges.evidence: Label warning, NHANES analyses, review; check B12 status before high-dose folate

edges.mechanism: Betaine remethylates homocysteine via BHMT independent of B12-dependent methionine synthase; additive tHcy lowering.
edges.evidence: MA of 5 RCTs (-1.23 umol/L with >=4 g/d betaine); interaction not directly tested

edges.mechanism: In VITACOG, B-vitamin slowing of cognitive decline in MCI occurred only with good baseline omega-3 (DHA) status.
edges.evidence: Post-hoc analysis of RCT (n=266); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Early claim that ascorbate destroys food B12 in vitro was not reproduced with standard assays; no clinically relevant interaction shown.
edges.evidence: Two in vitro studies, conflicting; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: High-dose cyanocobalamin-containing B-vitamin therapy accelerated GFR decline and increased vascular events; proposed cyanide/thiocyanate accumulation at GFR<50 (methylcobalamin/hydroxocobalamin suggested).
edges.evidence: DIVINe RCT (GFR MD -5.8; composite HR 2.0); narrative reviews; MA shows benefit only with normal renal function

edges.mechanism: Label: early Leber's disease patients given cyanocobalamin suffered severe and swift optic atrophy.
edges.evidence: FDA label warning; cohort showing higher B12 deficiency prevalence in carriers

edges.mechanism: Immediate hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis to cyanocobalamin or hydroxocobalamin injections; some tolerate alternative form.
edges.evidence: Label contraindication; UK multicentre series (8/29 anaphylaxis)

edges.mechanism: Lack of intrinsic factor requires lifelong high-dose oral (>=1 mg/d) or IM replacement; associated gastric NET/adenocarcinoma risk.
edges.evidence: NICE NG239; Cochrane oral vs IM; cohort of AG/PA neoplasia

edges.mechanism: High serum B12 after injection causes false-positive IF antibody radioassay (24 h after 1 mg; unreliable >3500 pg/mL).
edges.evidence: Assay method study

edges.mechanism: Supplement intake raises serum B12 (sample before treatment); anti-IF antibodies can cause falsely normal competitive-binding B12 results; total B12 includes inactive holoHC.
edges.evidence: NICE guidance, case report, biomarker reviews

edges.mechanism: Red-coloured hydroxocobalamin at antidote concentrations interferes with 27/77 analytes.
edges.evidence: In vitro spiking study

edges.mechanism: Cubilin variant increases risk of metformin-induced B12 deficiency (AA vs GG OR 2.43).
edges.evidence: GWAS in UK Biobank replicated in Scottish and DPPOS cohorts

edges.mechanism: Non-secretor variant alters serum B12 via holo-haptocorrin, not bioactive holoTC; serum B12 may misclassify status.
edges.evidence: GWAS and mechanistic study

edges.mechanism: GG genotype lowers holoTC; associated with neuropathy in elders, especially with folate intake >800 ug/d.
edges.evidence: Cross-sectional (n=171); low certainty
